hero.title: Charles Schwab Challenge
hero.description: Ludvig Aberg towers over this Charles Schwab Challenge field with a massive +2.04 SG Total and an 8.8% model win probability — more than double the next closest competitor — making him the clear alpha play at +1039. Below him, a cluster of value emerges in the +3000 to +4000 range: J.J. Spaun ranks #3 in overall strokes gained (+1.27) and #2 in SG Approach (+0.83) at +3547, while Ben Griffin — the defending champion — leads the field in putting (+0.56 SG Putting) and carries a 3.2% model win probability at +3068. With Colonial Country Club rewarding precision ball-striking and putting on small, undulating greens, this week's data points to a clear hierarchy of value plays beneath Aberg's dominance.

cards.title: Aberg Is the Unquestioned Top Dog
cards.description: Ludvig Aberg's +2.04 SG Total leads the field by a staggering 0.68 strokes over the next-best player, and his 8.8% model win probability dwarfs the implied 0.1% from his +1039 odds. He also ranks #1 in SG Approach at +0.86 — a critical skill at Colonial's tight, demanding approach shots.
cards.label: TOP DOG

cards.title: J.J. Spaun: Elite Ball-Striker at Value Odds
cards.description: Spaun ranks #3 in SG Total (+1.27) and #2 in SG Approach (+0.83), yet his +3547 odds imply far less than his 2.7% model win probability. After a T6 finish here in 2025, he has proven he can contend at Colonial when he avoids the cut — a boom-or-bust profile worth backing at this price.
cards.label: VALUE

cards.title: Defending Champ Griffin Leads in Putting
cards.description: Ben Griffin won this event in 2025 and leads the entire field in SG Putting at +0.56. His model win probability of 3.2% and +1.17 SG Total make him a legitimate contender at +3068, and his course history adjustment confirms his comfort level at Colonial.
cards.label: COURSE FIT

cards.title: Russell Henley Offers Best Risk-Reward
cards.description: Henley's +1.36 SG Total ranks #2 in the field and his 4.3% model win probability is the second-highest, yet he sits at +2247. He also ranks #5 in SG Approach (+0.53) and carries the best course fit adjustment among top contenders at +0.124, making him the most compelling outright value play on the board.
cards.label: VALUE

cards.title: Harry Hall Is the Primo Longshot
cards.description: At +5576, Harry Hall boasts a +0.90 SG Total (better than some players 50 spots shorter in odds), ranks #5 in SG Putting (+0.46), and carries a 16.1% top-10 probability. That top-10 number makes him a strong each-way or top-10 market play alongside his outright price.
cards.label: LONGSHOT

cards.title: Keegan Bradley: Hidden SG Profile at +5456
cards.description: Bradley's +0.86 SG Total matches players priced 20-30 spots shorter, and his 15.4% top-10 probability suggests he's being overlooked at +5456. Colonial's emphasis on accuracy and course management plays into his veteran skill set, making him a sneaky contender.
cards.label: LONGSHOT

cards.title: MacIntyre Pairs Putter with Recent Form
cards.description: Robert MacIntyre ranks #3 in SG Putting (+0.49) and #5 in SG Total (+1.25), with a T6 here in 2025 showing he's figured out Colonial. His 2.8% model win probability offers clear edge against his +3491 price, and his well-rounded game suits a course that demands no weaknesses.
cards.label: IN FORM

cards.title: Justin Thomas: Big Name, Real Value
cards.description: Thomas sits at #4 in SG Total (+1.25) with a 3.2% model win probability, yet +3017 odds significantly underrate his chances. While his -0.036 course fit is slightly negative, his elite ball-striking pedigree and comfort on tight, traditional courses make him a worthy play at this number.
cards.label: VALUE
